Revised assessment with literature context:
- Relative to standard policy rules (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor-type reactions), below-2% inflation and rising uncertainty imply a dovish tilt despite strong labor data.
- Softer business fixed investment aligns with the uncertainty-investment literature (Baker, Bloom, and Davis) and financing-constraint channels in the credit view (Gertler), pointing to downside risks to growth.
- Declines in market-based inflation compensation, with survey expectations “little changed,” are consistent with term-structure evidence that market prices embed lower inflation/growth risk premia (Ang and Piazzesi; Rudebusch and Wu), strengthening the case for easier policy to re-anchor expectations.
- The pledge to “act as appropriate” reflects forward-guidance tools in modern implementation (Goodfriend) and can ease financial conditions even without an immediate rate cut.

Overall tone: current conditions modestly positive, outlook cautious/dovish. sentiment score = 0.12
